river noun

classical

Traupman 206

flūmen, flūminis n.

noun, third declension

Other words

  • amnis, amnis m. — river, stream

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 206: flūmen, amnis (with no distinction as to size); Cic. Or. 39 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 372

    Lewis & Short: first a broad, swift-flowing water, so often a large river or a torrent in the poets.

  • fluvius, fluviī m. — river

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 206: tributary, fluvius

    A river in general; Traupman gives it for “tributary”, which it does not specially mean (fluviī in eum īnfluunt, rivers flow into it).

Examples

  • «Tagus est,» inquit pater, «quī Lisbōnam praeterfluit et ibi in mare effunditur.»

    “It’s the Tagus,” said Dad, “which flows past Lisbon and there pours into the sea.”Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

  • vadum candicāns

    rapidsTraupman 368

  • Tiberis monte Apennīnō (ex)oriēns

    the Tiber rising in the ApenninesTraupman 371

  • alveus

    the river bedTraupman 372

See also stream, bank.
